Jobs and Skills Australia Amendment Bill 2023

The government introduced the Jobs and Skills Australia Amendment Bill 2023 to establish Jobs and Skills Australia as a permanent, independent statutory body with tripartite governance—including union, employer and state/territory representation—to provide labour market and skills advice. The bill expands its functions to include workforce forecasting, regional analysis, studies on insecure work and disadvantage, and skills needs related to migration, clean energy and foundation skills, alongside existing investments such as $6.3 billion for vocational education in 2022-23, 480,000 fee-free TAFE places, and 10,000 New Energy Apprenticeships.
National Vocational Education and Training Regulator (Data Streamlining) Amendment Bill 2023

The National Vocational Education and Training Regulator (Data Streamlining) Amendment Bill 2023 was introduced to modernise VET data collection, reducing reporting lags of up to 20 months to improve responsiveness to skills shortages. The bill enables streamlined data obligations, authorises ICT system operators to access VET data, and supports 180,000 fee-free TAFE places and the $50 million TAFE Technology Fund.
Charter of the United Nations Amendment Bill 2021

Labor supported the Charter of the United Nations Amendment Bill 2021, which requires counterterrorism financial sanctions listings to be made by legislative instrument, condemned the Kabul airport terrorist attack that killed at least 60 people, and called on the government to ensure safety for Afghan nationals who assisted Australian troops.
